author: greywind5
text:
Studying this next diamond has been very informative to me. I've learnt that when you want to get onboard a trade, you will try to find reasons to justify your trade and convince yourself this is a good one, even if those reasons are totally made up.

I opened my chart and saw this DM setup. Problem is: it wasn't at an important level. So I went left and looked for a level. Couldn't find one. At this point if you trade live and you're a bad trader, you'll get frustrated because you finally found a QM (or a DM) but can't find which level it corresponds to. So you create it. You go find a meaningless FL that has been broken twice in the past and use this as your level. You trade the QM: it fails. But it's ok you say, the QM failed because the real move is a DM! And you will take the DM. What next? If the DM fails, I'll say "oh, it's because it was part of a bigger Gartley", which itself is part of a bigger QM?

This shows the importance of reading the market; seeing is not reading.
